name: BridgeDb
what: Maps identifiers between biological databases, so that one gene or metabolite can be recognised across resources that each name it differently.

name: WikiPathways
what: An open, community-curated pathway database. The department maintains its semantic layer and the clients most people actually use.

name: PathVisio
what: Desktop editor for biological pathways, and the origin of the GPML format.

name: Chemistry Development Kit
what: Java library for cheminformatics: structure handling, fingerprints, descriptors. Widely used well beyond this department.

name: Bacting
what: Scriptable cheminformatics and bioinformatics, usable from Java and Python.

name: ArrayAnalysis
what: Transcriptomics analysis workflows and quality control for microarray and RNA-seq data.

name: R-ODAF
what: Reproducible RNA-seq differential expression analysis, packaged as a Shiny app for regulatory toxicogenomics.

name: Virtual Human Platform
what: The VHP4Safety portal: a single entry point to the chemical safety assessment services the consortium runs.

name: AOP-Wiki RDF
what: Converts the AOP-Wiki to RDF, versions every release as its own named graph, and serves it over a public SPARQL endpoint with a query interface and dashboard.

name: molAOP Builder and Analyser
what: Maps Adverse Outcome Pathway key events onto molecular pathways, and analyses the resulting molecular AOPs.

name: pyBiodatafuse
what: Queries many biomedical databases at once and merges what comes back into a single knowledge graph, so a gene or compound list can be annotated from all of them in one step.

name: pysec2pri
what: Generates and use secondary identifier and symbol/label mapping sets for life sciences databases.

name: rdfsolve
what: Mine typed RDF schemas, convert between formats, and derive cross-dataset mappings.
